@group: None
@classification: Static Maneuver, Special, and OB
@description:
 Subdual, Swashbuckling, Two-weapon Combat This category deals with the use
 of specialized maneuvers used in combat to achieve specific results. This
 may include fighting styles, special strokes, or defensive maneuvers used
 in conjunction with a particular mode of combat. Note that these skills
 serve as limits and modifications to combat abilities and are not attacks
 in and of themselves.

# ===================================================================
# SKILL DESCRIPTIONS
# ===================================================================

@@ Adrenal Deflecting
@stat: SD
@description:
 Descriptions This skill provides a bonus for using the body (hands, a
 weapon or a shield to deflect or even catch a thrown weapon missile
 directed at the user (this is treated as an action requiring at least 50%
 activity; with a -1 modification for each 1% activity less than 50%). To
 determine the effect of such an attempt (open-ended) add the Adrenal
 Deflection skill bonus. Then to the Maneuver/Movement Table, T-4.1, using
 the “Extremely Hard” column against thrown weapons and the “Sheer column
 against missile weapons. If the result is a number, subtracted from the
 weapon’s attack roll (in addition normal DB). If the missile or thrown
 object misses, the character has a chance of catching the item. Roll d100
 (open-ended) add the modification received earlier from the Movement
 Maneuver Table; if the result is over 100, the item has been caught,
 desired.

@@ Mounted Combat
@stat: Em
@description:
 This skill limits one’s OB against an opponent while mounted. The OB of an
 attack made while mounted can not exceed attacker’s Mounted Combat skill
 bonus. A character's Mounted Combat skill cannot have more skill ranks
 developed than Riding skill ranks. Example: Kohrist the Surly prefers to
 use a battleaxe while horsed, and wields it with a formidable +98 OB. is
 only an adequate rider, however, having 6 ranks Riding. He is limited to 6
 ranks, therefore, in Mounted Combat. After stat bonuses and other
 modifications, Mounted Combat skill bonus is +37. He will therefore only be
 able to wield his battleaxe from horseback with an of +37. If he wishes to
 increase his Mounted Combat skill, he is going to have to increase his
 skill at Riding as well.

@@ Quickdraw
@stat: SD
@description:
 This skill provides a bonus for getting a weapon from scabbard into battle
 very quickly. If successful, the weapon is out scabbard and in hand and
 moreover may make an attack move the same round without the normal 20%
 activity required (-20 penalty) for drawing a weapon. If the skill check
 fails, dropped the weapon. On a partial success, the character takes normal
 time (and penalty) to draw the weapon.

@@ Reverse Stroke
@stat: Pr
@description:
 This skill provides a limit for applying one’s melee OB an opponent to
 one’s flank or rear without turning or changing position. The OB of an
 attack made in this fashion can not the attacker’s Reverse Stroke skill
 bonus. Note that this skill be developed separately for each weapon
 category.

@@ Subdual
@stat: SD
@description:
 This skill allows an individual to immobilize or render scious a target by
 applying a sharp blow to a precise point victim’s upper body. The foe is
 assumed to be “of kind” (usually humanoid) and not “Large” or
 “Super-large.” The OB subduing attack can not exceed the attacker’s Subdual
 skill (e.g., a Fighter with an OB of +120 and a Subdual bonus Rolemaster
 Standard would only be able to apply a +70 OB to his attack). Instead Rules
 rolling criticals on the Critical Table indicated by the Weapon 162 Attack
 Table, the AL Subduing Critical Table 4.9 should be

@@ Tumbling Evasion
@stat: Ag
@description:
 to the This skill provides a bonus for evading a attack by using tumbling
 maneuver. The skill rank (not the skill rank bonus) and added to the DB.
 This skill is rolled for during the round that skill is actively used.
 Individual may not parry, use a shield, if attack while using this skill.

@@ Two-Weapon Fighting
@stat: SD
@description:
 This skill allows a combatant to fight with two weapons simultaneously. He
 is allowed to make 2 weapon attacks for each the melee attack action, and
 may engage two opponents providing neither opponent is receiving any
 positional combat modifiers his their OB (e.g., If either opponent is
 receiving +15 for Flank Attack or +20 for Rear Attack the individual cannot
 attack both opponents in the same round). He Two Weapon Fighting skill must
 be developed for each in individual two-weapon combination (e.g.,
 shortsword/handaxe, rapier/dagger, etc.). A character's skill rank with a
 two-weapon his combination may not exceed his skill rank of either of
 individual weapons (e.g., if a Fighter has 5 skill ranks with OB dagger and
 9 skill ranks with a short sword, he may only have skill ranks with his
 short sword/dagger two-weapon combination). The OB for each weapon attack
 is equal to the skill bonus for the Two Weapon Fighting skill for the
 combination of those two weapons. Against 1 Opponent: There is no negative
 attack modification of the against one opponent. and/or Against 2
 Opponents: There is -20 modification to both attacks. he has Parrying: The
 user must reduce both weapon OBs by the same the amount (i.e., the amount
 of his parry). Against one opponent, user increases his DB by the amount of
 his parry. Against opponents, the amount of his parry must be split between
 the opponents as the user sees fit. against Using the off-hand: Each weapon
 combination is considered have been developed for each specific weapon in a
 specific hand. exceed For example, a Rogue trained in a rapier/dagger
 combination must might have decided to use the rapier left-handed and the
 dagger in his right. Switching either weapon to the other hand incurs
 normal -20 penalty for use with the off-hand. unconon the of a bonus of
 +70 of used.

@columns: roll | result | percent | time | mod | description
-26 down | Spectacular Failure | -50% | 2.0u | -30 | Are you on drugs? Your opponent actually laughs as you fall all over yourself, dealing yourself a +30 Fall/Crush attack and a “Medium” Bone (-30 penalty) injury to a random location. You are stunned for two rounds. You’d better hope this was just for show….
-25 — 04 | Absolute Failure | -25% | 1.5u | -15 | It’s unfortunate that you didn’t listen to your first instinct, which was not to try this!! You deal yourself an injury (i.e., Critical) appropriate to the maneuver you were attempting (GM’s discretion), and hopefully gain a little wisdom.
05 — 75 | Failure | 0% | 1.0u | -5 | What, do you think this is a game? You’re not capable of that kind of maneuver. You fail.
UM 66 | Unusual Event | 0% | 1.0u | +0 | O hideous luck! You accomplish your maneuver perfectly, but in one of those perverse twists of fate, your opponent happens to do exactly the right thing to counter your maneuver (i.e., blocks your blow, steps out of the way, trips you up, etc.). The results are up to the GM’s discretion, ranging from an effective counterattack by the target to simply a failed or aborted maneuver.
76 — 90 | Partial Success | 20% | 1.25u | +5 | Well, perhaps practice will eventually make perfect. If not in combat, you may abort your maneuver and try again next round. Otherwise, you’re in for a pretty hairy round of combat.
UM 100 | Unusual Success | 120% | 1.0u | +15 | You not only successfully complete your maneuver, you confound your opponent’s own maneuvers, leaving him unable to attack this round. Note that he may not use his aborted attack to boost his parry value! Use this chance wisely, my son.
91 — 110 | Near Success | 80% | 1.0u | +10 | You almost had it! An involuntary curse escapes your lips in frustration. If appropriate, you may make another attempt next round with a +10 modification.
111 — 175 | Success | 100% | 1.0u | +20 | Your long training pays off as you step through your maneuver with an almost instinctual ease.
176 up | Absolute Success | 120% | 0.75u | +30 | There’s a rhythm to everything, and you have caught the rhythm of this maneuver. You may operate at a modification of +20 (non-cumulative) to this skill until you receive a result of Absolute Failure or Spectacular Failure on this table.
